newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - New issues fly, JP Morgan sags.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - New issues fly, JP Morgan sags.

text.p: New issue activity dominated the U.S. corporate bond market on Wednesday, with spreads in the secondary market remaining firm, but closing mostly unchanged, market players said.

Among individual credits, J.P. Morgan & Co bonds widened slightly as Moody's Investors Service placed the bank's debt on Creditwatch negative. High-yield credits in the paging sector were also stronger on positive earnings news, traders said.
Issuers sold over $2.0 billion in investment-grade bonds and over $500 million in high-yield bonds on Wednesday.
The flood of high-grade supply was triggered by opportunistic issuers, seeking to take advantage of the continuing Treasury rally, syndicate sources said.

The most prominent example was IBM Corp which quickly sold $1.0 billion in 10-year and 30-year debt via Morgan Stanley & Co. The 10-year paper priced at a spread of 44 basis points over comparable Treasuries, while the 30-year paper priced at a 19 basis-point spread.
Other issuers were Weyerhaeuser Co $300 million deal, Hercules Inc $200 million deal and Avon Products Inc $100 million 144a offering.
Elsewhere, Moody's placed the debt of J.P. Morgan on downgrade watch on Wednesday after the bank announced it planned to purchase 45 percent stake in American Century Cos, an asset managment company.
J.P. Morgan bond spreads widened one to two basis points on the news. Analysts called the price change significant given currently tight spreads among high-grade credits.
Andrew Gilligan, high-grade bank debt analyst at Bear Stearns & Co said spreads could widen "a few more basis points," if Moody's cut JP Morgan ratings, which he expected.
Among Wednesday's high-yield issuers, Primus Telecommunications Group increased the size of its deal to $225 million from $125 million to meet strong demand.
Lehman Brothers Inc, the lead underwriter, priced the B3/B-minus-rated deal at par to yield 11.75 percent.
The bonds were heard trading 102-102.5 later in the day.
The offering from the Vienna-based long distance telephone provider included a three-year prefunded interest reserve, as well as warrants to purchase 1.8 percent of the company.
He believed J.P. Morgan's ratings would be downgraded to reflect the increased risk associated with investment banking activities, which consitute a growing part of the bank's business strategy.

In other trading news, Arch Communications Group Inc's zero coupon bonds rose as high as 61-62 from their opening level of 56 as the paging company released better-than-expected cash flow figures for the second quarter.
The positive news lifted prices in other paging sector credits in the high-yield market. Archer's bonds closed at 60 bid level, a trader said.
In other markets, the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 80 points to 8255, the third consecutive all-time high for the blue chip average.
Stocks echoed the Treasury market which ended the day sharply higher on heavy broad-based buying.
The 30-year bond fell to 6.32 percent, its lowest yield since the February 16, 1996 close.
-Douglas Brown, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-859-1662
